title: StreamGaze: Gaze-Guided Temporal Reasoning and Proactive Understanding in Streaming Videos
abstract: arXiv:2512.01707v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Streaming video understanding requires models not only to process temporally incoming frames, but also to anticipate user intent for realistic applications such as Augmented Reality (AR) glasses. While prior streaming benchmarks evaluate temporal reasoning, none measure whether Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can interpret or leverage human gaze signals within a streaming setting. To fill this gap, we introduce StreamGaze, the first benchmark designed to evaluate how effectively MLLMs utilize gaze for temporal and proactive reasoning in streaming videos. StreamGaze introduces gaze-guided past, present, and proactive tasks that comprehensively assess streaming video understanding. Past and present tasks require immediate responses based on observations available at query time, whereas proactive tasks require models to continuously process incoming frames and respond at the appropriate future moment. translated_abstract: 流式视频理解要求模型不仅能够按时间顺序处理连续到来的视频帧，还需要预判用户意图，以满足增强现实（AR）眼镜等现实应用场景的需求。尽管现有的流式基准测试已对时序推理能力进行了评估，但尚无任何基准衡量多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）能否在流式环境中解读或利用人类视线（gaze）信号。为填补这一空白，我们提出了StreamGaze，这是首个专门评估MLLMs在流式视频中利用视线进行时序推理与主动式推理能力的基准。StreamGaze引入了视线引导的过去、现在和主动式任务，对流式视频理解进行全面评估。其中，过去和现在任务要求模型基于查询时刻可获得的观察立即做出响应，而主动式任务则要求模型持续处理不断到来的视频帧，并在合适的未来时机做出响应。为了构建StreamGaze，
tldr: StreamGaze是首个评估多模态大语言模型能否在流式视频中利用人类视线信号进行时序推理与主动式响应的基准，通过视线引导的过去、现在和主动式三类任务全面检验流式视频理解能力。
en_tdlr: StreamGaze is the first benchmark evaluating how effectively MLLMs can leverage human gaze signals for temporal reasoning and proactive responding in streaming videos, through gaze-guided past, present, and proactive tasks.
